name: TPS22917DBVR
title: TPS22917, TPS22917L: 2 A, 80 mΩ load switch for 1 V to 5.5 V with very low leakage, adjustable slew rate and output discharge
summary: A single-channel load switch on a P-channel MOSFET for 1 V to 5.5 V rails and up to 2 A continuous, 80 mΩ typical at 5 V. A capacitor on CT sets the output slew rate and so the inrush, and a resistor on QOD sets how fast the output is discharged when off. Reverse current is blocked whenever the switch is on. It draws 0.5 µA on and 10 nA off (typical); the TPS22917 is enabled by ON high and the TPS22917L by ON low, both in a 6-pin SOT-23.
key_figures: 80 mΩ typ at 5 V, 120 mΩ at 1.8 V, 220 mΩ at 1 V (25 °C, 200 mA)
100 µs at 5 V with CT open; 4 µs/pF with CT ≥ 100 pF
activates at -0.5 A typ; reverse leakage 1 µA max
VIH 1 V min, VIL 0.35 V max; 750 kΩ smart pulldown

notes: TPS22917 order codes turn on with ON high; TPS22917L order codes turn on with ON low. Within each, the codes differ in reel size, lead finish and the ordering temperature range.

pins.name: ON
pins.function: Switch control: turns the switch on when high on the TPS22917 (low on the TPS22917L). Must not float.

pins.name: CT
pins.function: Slew-rate control. A capacitor from CT to VIN slows the output ramp and lengthens the turn-on time; with CT open the timing is fastest.

pins.name: QOD
pins.function: Quick output discharge. Tied straight to VOUT it discharges the output through the internal resistance; through an external resistor to VOUT it discharges through the sum of both; left open, no discharge takes place.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: One TPS22917 switches a supply rail through to a downstream load. CT, from VIN to the CT pin, sets how fast VOUT ramps and so the inrush into CL; RQOD, between VOUT and QOD, sets how fast the output discharges once the switch turns off. CIN holds up the supply during switch-on. Values are those of the design example: 3.6 V in, 47 µF and 1 kΩ load, inrush below 150 mA and fall time of at least 40 ms.

parts.note: input capacitance; 1 µF is enough in most cases, a slow supply may need more bulk capacitance
slew-rate capacitor for a 150 mA inrush limit into 47 µF at 3.6 V; rated 7 V or more
external discharge resistor for a fall time of at least 40 ms

circuits.title: Test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit the switching characteristics are measured in: the supply with CIN at VIN, CT from VIN to the CT pin, a step on ON, and at the output CL and RL with RQOD from VOUT to QOD. Turn-off and fall times are set by the load time constant, (RQOD + QOD || RL) × CL, since the internal QOD resistance is switched in when the device is off.

operation.text: A 2 A load switch for 1 V to 5.5 V built on a P-channel MOSFET, with its gate driver, charge pump, control logic, reverse-current blocking and output discharge FET inside. Its own blocks are the reverse-current blocking on the IN–OUT path, control logic and driver from ON, timing control on CT, and the discharge path on QOD. Off, it draws very little from VIN or the downstream rail.

ON works with standard GPIO logic levels. The TPS22917 turns on when ON is above VIH; the TPS22917L turns on when ON is below VIL. While ON sits at or below VIL a smart pulldown of about 750 kΩ holds the pin low so it does not float during power-up sequencing; once ON is driven to VIH or above the pulldown is disconnected and the pin leaks at most 10 nA.

A capacitor from CT to VIN slows VOUT's rise. The ramp on CT ends a little after VOUT reaches its final level. With CT open the slew rate is highest and turn-on fastest (72 mV/µs and 100 µs typical at 5 V). Turn-on time scales with CT through the µs/pF constants of the switching characteristics, slew rate inversely through the (mV/µs)·pF constants. CT must be rated at least 7 V.

tON runs from ON crossing VIH to VOUT reaching 90%; tDELAY from ON crossing VIH to VOUT at 10%; tRISE from 10% to 90% of VOUT, and SRON is the steepest VOUT slope within it. tOFF runs from ON crossing VIL to VOUT falling to 90%; tFALL from 90% to 10% of VOUT.

QOD can be tied straight to VOUT, so the output discharges through the internal resistance (150 Ω typical) when the switch turns off; connected to VOUT through an external RQOD, so it discharges through QOD + RQOD; or left open, so the output floats when off. Fall time follows the discharge resistance, the load resistance and the load capacitance.

Output discharge also works when the system supply is taken away, so it can sequence a system's power-down. As VIN decays with the input capacitor, below some level the discharge path weakens, and charge left on the output capacitor then takes longer to drain.

Reverse blocking is always active while the switch is on. When VOUT is above VIN and the reverse current passes IRCB (–0.5 A typical), the switch turns off within tRCB (10 µs typical) and stays off, blocking current through both the FET and its body diode, for as long as VOUT is held above VIN. When VOUT falls back under the VRCB release level (25 mV typical) the switch turns on again with its controlled slew rate.

Divide the inrush limit by the load capacitance to get the largest slew rate, then the slew-rate constant by that rate to get the smallest CT. The resulting turn-on must also stay within the IMAX and IPLS ratings.

With one switch per rail, the QOD resistance of each sets that rail's fall time, so the rails go down in the order and with the margins the powered device asks for. Find the discharge resistance from the wanted fall time, then subtract the internal QOD to get RQOD.

The supply range is 1 V to 5.5 V. The source wants good regulation, a short path to VIN, and enough capability for the load's current steps. A 1 µF CIN normally holds VIN up as the switch closes; extra bulk capacitance is needed with a slow source or large load steps.

Short traces throughout; CIN and the output capacitor right at the device; wide VIN, VOUT and GND traces, all to limit parasitic inductance. In the example layout CIN sits beside VIN and GND, RQOD beside VOUT and QOD, CT is placed above the package with its trace run round to the CT pin, and ON is routed out to the GPIO.
Junction temperature is limited to 125°C in normal use; the allowed dissipation at a given ambient follows from θJA, which depends heavily on the board.
